purpose: Executable acceptance inventory for sanitized, guarded U6 fresh-schema, legacy-upgrade, two-pass idempotence, and forward-and-restore rehearsal. This manifest never authorizes a production connection, provider traffic, or a reverse migration.

requiredRows: colliding canonical meta and legacy muse-spark accounts sharing the same logical account tuple
colliding combo slots that exercise survivor-owned and lowest-logical-slot-id keeper rules
colliding usage windows that exercise survivor-owned keeper and settled-state merge rules
requests, usage snapshots, usage windows, combo membership exclusions, and device setup jobs referencing discarded account ids
managed combo enrollment rules, family assignment, and membership exclusions
one active model-scoped usage window and one inactive account-wide historical usage window
same-timestamp active and inactive usage snapshots, with the later append inactive
fixtureContract.sourceImmutability: fingerprint the pre-migration legacy source before its backup/dump and require the same fingerprint after candidate migration
fixtureContract.sqliteBackupSemantics: runMigrations' built-in SQLite backup is best-effort: a backup error is warned and migration proceeds. This rehearsal independently creates and verifies an immutable source copy before candidate mutation, so this acceptance run is externally backup-protected but the production migration itself is not backup-gated.
fixtureContract.idempotence: run every candidate migration twice; the second pass creates no duplicate rows and changes no adopted schema or data outcome
fixtureContract.safety: Exact test-only identities, disposable loopback PostgreSQL targets, immutable source backups/dumps, generated child schemas, and distinct rollback restores are required.

usageSnapshots.generator: usage_snapshots_append_order_seq nextval is the atomic database-generated append-order allocator

legacyUpgradeAssertions.assertion: The seeded upgrade source genuinely has usage_snapshots without active or append_order; migration backfills active to 1 and allocates unique durable append_order values before post-migration inserts.

Fresh and upgraded SQLite schemas use INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT. Fresh and upgraded PostgreSQL schemas use BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT atomic nextval from usage_snapshots_append_order_seq plus idx_usage_snapshots_append_order uniqueness. The durable account/window/timestamp/append_order lookup index exists in both dialects.

meta and muse-spark collisions collapse to one canonical meta account exactly once. Survivor selection is deterministic: latest last_used, then latest refresh_token_issued_at, then latest created_at, then lowest logical account id. Freshest credential fields come from one deterministic row; API keys and nullable state use the same logical-id-safe ordering.

Colliding combo slots retain a survivor-owned keeper when present; otherwise the lowest logical slot id wins. In both cases enabled wins and the lowest numeric priority wins before discarded account ids are repointed.

Colliding usage windows retain a survivor-owned keeper when present; the latest and most-complete closed row supplies settled fields, while earliest start, maximum utilization, and earliest 100% observation are preserved across aliases.

combo_slots, requests, usage_snapshots, usage_windows, combo_membership_exclusions, and device_setup_jobs that reference discarded ids are repointed before deletion; exclusion collisions preserve the survivor-owned row.
Both migration passes preserve canonical meta state, adopted catalog and rows, revision singleton/triggers, managed routing rows, and indexes without duplicate outcomes.

repositoryAndRetentionAssertions.assertion: A newest inactive marker makes getLatestSnapshot return null. Active chart series omit inactive rows, while unfiltered getRawSnapshots retains complete history.
For equal timestamps, getLatestSnapshot selects the later database-generated append_order rather than a physical storage location.
Retention deletes only eligible old raw snapshots by durable append_order and preserves the current snapshot.
Managed enrollment rules, exclusions, assignments, slots, and routing revision reads round-trip; a policy mutation advances the revision.

rollbackFingerprints.algorithm: catalog plus sanitized fixture/adopted rows plus repository and retention smoke outputs
rollbackFingerprints.source: capture with legacy-schema queries before backup/dump; these queries never reference active or append_order
rollbackFingerprints.artifact: checksum every SQLite backup and PostgreSQL dump before restore
rollbackFingerprints.candidate: fresh and upgraded catalogs plus post-migration data/repository fingerprints after two passes must satisfy this manifest
rollbackFingerprints.rollback: restore the immutable pre-migration fixture backup or dump into a distinct clean target; its legacy-source fingerprint must equal the original source fingerprint
rollbackFingerprints.forbidden: No production connection, production data, provider request, reverse meta-to-muse-spark migration, or reverse-schema migration is a rollback strategy.
